answer.title: Check rules with ruff and against any revision in krrood check
answer.body:
## Why

<!-- github-workflow:why:start -->
`krrood check` enforced only part of AGENTS.md and ran only in pre-commit, so a break of a rule a script can check reached review unless the author's own hook caught it. Checking fifteen more rules through ruff, and running the check in CI on the lines a pull request changes, catches those breaks before a reviewer has to point them out.
<!-- github-workflow:why:end -->

<details>
<summary>What changes, how it is tested, and what breaks</summary>

<!-- github-workflow:changes:start -->
## What this changes

`krrood check` enforces more of `AGENTS.md`, and it now also runs in CI, on the lines a pull request changes.

- **`RuffRuleChecker`** (`krrood/development_tools/agents/ruff_rules.py`): a rule can now be enforced by lint rules of ruff. The checker selects exactly the codes the rule names and runs ruff `--isolated` with settings passed on the command line, so every repository using krrood checks alike. Each rule declares whether it covers tests, the code they test, or both.
- **Fifteen rules are now checked by ruff:**
  - mutable defaults of arguments and dataclass fields (`B006`, `RUF008`)
  - `assert` outside tests (`S101`)
  - type hint presence, outside tests (`ANN0xx`/`ANN2xx`)
  - builtin generics and imports from `typing_extensions` (`UP006`/`UP007`/`UP045`, banning `typing`)
  - postponed annotations (`I002`, `UP037`)
  - absolute imports outside tests (`TID252`)
  - no `unittest.TestCase` in tests (`PT009`, `PT027`, banned API)
  - imports before any other code (`E402`)
  - no `Protocol` interfaces (banned API)
  - no `raise Exception` and no messages worded where raised, outside tests (`TRY002`, `TRY003`)
  - no `global` statement (`PLW0603`)
  - no names of builtins or standard library modules (`A001`, `A002`, `A003`, `A005`)
  - no `else` after `return`/`raise`, no collapsible `if`, nesting at most five deep (`RET505`, `RET506`, `SIM102`, `PLR1702`)
  - no commented-out code (`ERA001`)
  - no import under `TYPE_CHECKING` used at runtime (`TC004`)
- **Rules are split** wherever a script checks only part of one, as the rule-modelling rule asks, so the checkable part carries the checker. The split rules are type hints, writing tests with pytest, imports at the top, interface segregation, guard clauses, constants, meaningful comments, and shadowing bound names.
- `PLR1702` is still a preview rule in ruff 0.17.2. Its checker alone enables preview, so no other rule's behaviour changes. Its limit of five nested blocks is ruff's default, and the rule text states it. The ruff checks pass `--target-version py310`, the oldest Python krrood's `requires-python` allows.
- **`krrood check --since REVISION`** checks the lines the working tree changes since a revision, staged or not. Without files it finds the tracked Python files changed since then itself.
- **`[tool.krrood.check] exclude`** in `pyproject.toml` lists the files the check leaves alone once (ORM interfaces, the checker tests' dataset and, for now, the ripple down rules expert answers), wherever the check runs. The duplicate `exclude` is removed from the pre-commit hook.
- **CI:** the `small_packages` job of `ci.yml` runs `krrood check --since HEAD^1` on pull requests right after installing the dependencies, before any test, and fails on any violation in the changed lines. A new `check_rules` input of `ci_reusable.yml` selects the job. A pull request is checked out as its merge commit, whose first parent is the base.
- `krrood/doc/development_tools.md` documents all of this.

Rules deliberately left unchecked for now:
- ruff's `TC001`–`TC003`: they would move imports that the ORM and serializers need at runtime. `TC004`, the reverse direction, is checked.
- The rule against imports inside functions (`PLC0415`): it conflicts with the core-boundary exception.
- `getattr` and `try`/`except`: these need custom AST checkers, because ruff covers `getattr` only partly and `try` not at all.
- Comparisons with bare numbers (`PLR2004`): dropped, because it flagged many comparisons that read fine, such as `len(args) == 2`.

## Existing violations

The checks report only the lines a change touches, so existing violations block nothing until their code is edited. Run over every tracked file, the rules find 5,001 today:

| Rule | Findings |
|---|---|
| Type hint presence (outside tests) | 2,772 |
| Postponed annotations | 723 |
| No `unittest.TestCase` in tests | 381 |
| No commented-out code | 262 |
| No `raise Exception` / messages worded where raised | 185 |
| No superfluous nesting | 183 |
| Builtin generics and `typing_extensions` | 175 |
| Imports before any other code | 133 |
| No `assert` outside tests | 75 |
| Absolute imports | 60 |
| No builtin names | 37 |
| No `Protocol` interfaces | 7 |
| No `global` statement | 7 |
| No runtime import under `TYPE_CHECKING` | 1 |
| No mutable defaults | 0 |

Two of these need follow-up work:
- **`Protocol` interfaces are not intended**, so they get no `noqa` and should be refactored onto explicit superclasses or mixins:
  - `krrood/src/krrood/exceptions.py`
  - `krrood/src/krrood/entity_query_language/verbalization/rendering/discourse.py`
  - `krrood/src/krrood/entity_query_language/verbalization/rendering/source_link_resolver.py`
  - `krrood/src/krrood/entity_query_language/verbalization/vocabulary/parts_of_speech.py`
  - `robokudo/src/robokudo/analysis_engine.py`
  - `robokudo/src/robokudo/subtree.py`
  - `robokudo/src/robokudo/scripts/query_test_client.py`

  `shipped_rules/design_principles.py` imports `Protocol` only to name it in the rule's text, so that import carries `# noqa: TID251`.
- **A likely bug the `TC004` check found:** `robokudo/src/robokudo/display.py` imports `Dot` from `pydot` only under `TYPE_CHECKING` (line 43), but `generate_pydot_graph` calls `Dot(graph_type="digraph")` at runtime (line 176). That call raises `NameError` unless something else binds `Dot` in the module.

## What breaks and how to migrate (`api-break`)

- **`CodeRulesCheck`'s field `staged` is renamed to `changed_lines`**, since it now also takes the since-a-revision mode. Its type widens from `StagedLines | None` to `ChangedLines | None`, the new base of `StagedLines` and `LinesChangedSince`. Migrate by replacing `CodeRulesCheck(..., staged=StagedLines(...))` with `CodeRulesCheck(..., changed_lines=StagedLines(...))`.
- **Shipped rules changed their wording**, and every repository's generated `AGENTS.md` changes with them. The changes:
  - `TypeHintsRules.ANNOTATE_EVERYTHING` no longer says "accurate". That is now the new rule `ACCURATE_TYPE_HINTS`.
  - `WritingTestsRules.WRITE_TESTS_WITH_PYTEST` no longer mentions `unittest`. That is now the new rule `NO_UNITTEST_TEST_CASES`.
  - `ImportsRules.IMPORTS_AT_THE_TOP` now reads "before any other code". The part about local imports is the new rule `NO_LOCAL_IMPORTS`.
  - The Interface Segregation detail no longer mentions `Protocol`. That is now the new rule `DesignPrinciplesRules.NO_PROTOCOLS`.
  - `CodeStyleRules.NO_MUTABLE_DEFAULT_ARGUMENTS` now covers dataclass field defaults too.
  - New checked rules sit next to the rules they come from: `NO_BUILTIN_NAMES`, `NO_SUPERFLUOUS_NESTING`, `RAISE_CUSTOM_EXCEPTIONS`, `NO_GLOBAL_STATEMENT`, `NO_COMMENTED_OUT_CODE` and `NO_RUNTIME_IMPORTS_UNDER_TYPE_CHECKING`.

  Migrate by running `krrood agents-md`.
- **The check now reports more.** A commit that touches code breaking one of the fifteen rules fails the `krrood-check` pre-commit hook and the CI step. A deliberate exception can be marked with ruff's own `# noqa: <code>` comment, which the ruff-backed checkers respect.

Please discuss this break with the krrood code owners in `.github/CODEOWNERS` or in the Cramgineers channel before requesting review. The CI step applies to every contributor.

## Tests

- Added 45 tests: the ruff checker, how test modules are recognised, each shipped ruff-checked rule against a dataset snippet whose expected findings are marked in it (and left alone in the modules it exempts), a `# noqa` exception, lines and files changed since a revision, and `--since` and the exclusions on the command line.
- `test_every_checker_krrood_ships_is_that_of_a_shipped_rule` now lists the fifteen new checkers. In its module, the shipped `DesignPrinciplesRules` is reached through its module, since a dataset mimic of the same name is imported there.
- The `git` helper and the `repository` fixture moved to a shared module and `conftest.py`.
- After merging the current `main`, all 146 development-tools tests pass, and `krrood agents-md --check`, `krrood skills --check` and `krrood issue-forms --check` pass.
- The branch's changed code passes `krrood check --since origin/main`.
- The CI step runs for the first time on this pull request.

Made with AI assistance
<!-- github-workflow:changes:end -->

</details>
